title: Track B: broker daemon and veil exec client
description:
Parent: Veil v1 epic. Depends on B1.

WHAT: 'veil sandbox' starts a broker (same binary, --broker mode) listening on a per-session unix socket under ~/.cmdrvl/state/veil/broker/<session>.sock (0600). Protocol: newline-delimited JSON {"tool":"shape","argv":[...],"cwd":...}; never a shell string. Broker checks tool basename against [spine] authorized_tools, resolves the binary via PATH captured at launch, refuses argv containing shell metacharacters that would need a shell, runs it with the operator's real permissions, streams {stream, chunk} frames and a final {exit_code}. Every call is audit-logged with enforcement:'sandbox', origin:'broker'.

CLIENT: 'veil exec <tool> [args]' inside the sandbox; also honor VEIL_BROKER_SOCKET. Hook remediation text inside a sandbox says 'run: veil exec shape <path>'.

SECURITY: the broker is the only privileged path; keep it tiny, no config reload, dies with the sandbox parent (SIGHUP/pidfd). Rate-limit and size-cap output (spine tools emit metadata; 16 MiB cap).

TESTS: protocol unit tests; integration test launching broker + client with a fake 'shape' script; rejection tests (unauthorized tool, shell metachars, path escape).

AMBITION ROUND ADDITIONS (2026-09-02): (a) FLAG POLICY: each authorized tool declares flags that raise its output label to protected (shape --explicit, rvl --raw, profile --dump, canon --show-values); the broker refuses them with reason broker_flag_forbidden. Without this the broker is cat with extra steps. Config: [spine.flags] shape = ["--explicit"] etc., with built-in defaults for the cmdrvl spine tools. (b) OUTPUT SCANNING: before returning stdout the broker runs the shared boundary-detectors packs (crate extracted in airlock bead al-34s; pinned dependency) and refuses (default) or redacts output that trips secrets/PII/tabular-dump detectors, recording the refusal with detector id and span hash. (c) DERIVED REGISTRY: every returned output (and any file the tool wrote under --out) is hashed and appended to ~/.cmdrvl/state/veil/derived.jsonl {hash, tool, argv_hash, session, ts}; the provenance allowlist bead consumes this. (d) LINUX: apply a seccomp filter to the sandboxed tree denying ptrace, process_vm_readv/writev and opening /proc/<pid>/mem so an adversarial agent cannot read broker memory; macOS relies on seatbelt's default debugging denial - document.

REFINEMENT ROUND 1 (2026-09-02): deliver 'veil exec <tool> [args]' DIRECT MODE first (no sandbox, no socket): validates tool + flag policy, runs the tool, scans output with boundary-detectors, registers output hashes in derived.jsonl, audits. This gives Track A the derived registry (bd-3qw) without waiting for the sandbox; the broker daemon is the same code path behind a socket. Step order: 1 direct mode, 2 socket protocol, 3 daemon lifecycle.

title: Track A: path-anywhere-in-argv rule replaces the reader allowlist
description:
Parent: Veil v1 epic.

PROBLEM: src/extract.rs only recognizes cat/bat/less/more/head/tail plus a few interpreters. awk 1 data/x.csv, sed -n p data/x.csv, base64/xxd/perl/jq/sqlite3/duckdb/grep/rg on a protected file are all ALLOWED (probe 2026-09-02). So are cp/tar/curl -F file=@ which move the bytes somewhere unguarded.

DESIGN: After shell decomposition (sibling bead), for every simple command: resolve each argv token that looks like a path (contains / or a known file extension, or resolves to an existing file relative to cwd) to an absolute path. If any resolved path is protected/sensitive under the existing classification, the command is resolved through policy UNLESS the command basename is in [spine] authorized_tools. The old reader list stays only as an explanation hint ('cat is a direct reader'). Keep the existing fast path: commands with no path-like tokens are allowed silently.

EDGE CASES: tokens like 2>/dev/null and dir> currently get logged as paths (see audit log) - the shell decomposer must strip redirections before argv resolution and treat '< protected' as a read (already denied). Ignore /dev/*, /proc/*. Never stat more than 64 tokens per command (perf budget < 1ms).

title: Track A: content-sniff classification via boundary-detectors
description:
Parent bd-30b. Depends on bd-29r; related to airlock al-34s (shared crate) and supersedes bd-28k (magic bytes).

title: veil doctor's dcg-hook check requires exact 'Bash' matcher, but dcg installs under 'Bash|PowerShell'
description:
veil doctor's hooks check (inspect_dcg_entries in src/hooks.rs) does exact string equality on the PreToolUse entry's matcher field, only recognizing a matcher literally equal to "Bash" (matcher_matches(entry, "Bash") called from inspect_dcg_entries, src/hooks.rs ~L144-161; exact-eq matcher_matches at ~L270-275).

dcg's own installer (dcg install) registers its hook under the combined matcher "Bash|PowerShell" in a single PreToolUse entry, which functionally covers Bash calls but never satisfies veil's exact-match check. Result: veil doctor permanently reports 'missing dcg Bash hook' / status action_needed even when dcg is correctly installed and working, which cascades into cins's guard preflight (required_guards: [dcg, veil], both must report ok=true) refusing to run at all.

Reproduced 2026-08-31: dcg doctor reported hook_wiring=ok with the hook under 'Bash|PowerShell'; veil doctor simultaneously reported hooks=action_needed / 'missing dcg Bash hook'. Restarting Claude Code (to pick up hook config changes) did not fix it -- the settings.json shape never satisfies veil's check regardless of restart.

Attempted workaround: added a second PreToolUse entry with matcher exactly "Bash" pointing at the same dcg command, alongside the existing "Bash|PowerShell" entry. This satisfied veil doctor (hooks=ok) but broke dcg doctor's own hook_wiring check ('Found 2 dcg hook entries (expected 1)', status=warning). Neither tool's own remediation path produces a state both doctors accept simultaneously. Reverted the workaround; no fix currently exists at the settings.json level.

Fix needs to happen in one of the two tools:
- veil: relax inspect_dcg_entries's matcher_matches to recognize any matcher string containing "Bash" (e.g. "Bash", "Bash|PowerShell"), not just exact-equal "Bash", OR
- dcg: register two separate PreToolUse entries (exact "Bash" and exact "PowerShell") instead of one combined entry, and reconcile dcg doctor's hook_wiring count check to allow that shape.

Blocks: email-triage's cins guard preflight, and presumably any other cins invocation on this machine.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 0875ac5 (main): matcher_matches now treats a PreToolUse matcher as a pipe-delimited alternation instead of exact string equality, so dcg's real Bash|PowerShell matcher is recognized. Verified against live ~/.claude/settings.json with a source build (veil doctor now reports healthy). Live installed binary is via Homebrew (0.4.0); needs a tagged release + brew bump to reach the installed binary -- source fix is complete and pushed.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
Corroborating evidence (2026-08-31): src/hooks.rs L9 defines MANAGED_MATCHERS = ["Read", "Grep", "Bash"] -- veil always installs itself as three separate single-tool matcher entries, never a combined "Read|Grep|Bash" string. inspect_dcg_entries's exact-equality matcher_matches(entry, "Bash") check (L144-161, L270-275) was clearly written against that same assumption: every managed hook, including a well-behaved third-party one, was expected to register under a bare tool-name matcher. dcg is the only participant that deviates by combining Bash+PowerShell into one pipe-delimited matcher string, which is why it's the one hook veil can never find.

This confirms the fix belongs on veil's side rather than being an arbitrary policy call: matcher_matches should treat a managed hook as covering "Bash" if the entry's matcher is Bash-only OR a pipe-delimited group containing "Bash" as one of its alternatives (mirroring how Claude Code itself parses `"Bash|PowerShell"` as an alternation, not a literal string). Suggest changing matcher_matches (or adding a dedicated matcher_covers_tool helper) to split on `|` and check membership, then reuse it for both inspect_dcg_entries and the existing managed-hook matcher inspection so future combined-matcher hooks don't hit the same false negative.

title: veil has no protocol adapter for Grok -- every Grok filesystem tool call is hard-blocked
description:
dcg already supports a native Grok integration: 'dcg install --grok' installs the dcg PreToolUse hook for Grok at ~/.grok/hooks/dcg.json (user-level) or ./.grok/hooks/dcg.json (--project), noting Grok also picks up dcg via the Claude-Code compatibility layer but the native path gives cleaner doctor output.

veil has no equivalent -- 'veil install' only writes managed PreToolUse hooks into Claude Code's settings.json (see install_into_path / install_matcher_hook in src/hooks.rs); there's no --grok flag and no ~/.grok/hooks/veil.json path. Grok sessions relying on veil's data-exfiltration guard currently only get it via the Claude-Code compatibility layer, if Grok reads that file at all, with no native install/doctor support to verify it.

Request: add 'veil install --grok' (and corresponding uninstall/doctor support) writing veil's PreToolUse hook(s) to ~/.grok/hooks/veil.json (or --project ./.grok/hooks/veil.json), mirroring dcg's pattern so agent guard coverage is consistent across dcg and veil for Grok sessions.
close_reason: Fixed in commit b86ab28 (main): added HookProtocol::Grok with payload detection (hookEventName=="pre_tool_use" or toolName in run_terminal_command/run_terminal_cmd), a dedicated camelCase parser (toolName/toolInput/cwd/sessionId), tool-name normalization (read_file->Read, grep->Grep, run_terminal_command|run_terminal_cmd->Bash), and output rendering reusing Gemini's decision/reason JSON shape (byte-identical to Grok's documented contract). Verified end-to-end with a release build against real Grok wire-format payloads for Read, Grep, and Bash tools, both allow and deny outcomes, including a protected-directory deny for the Bash case. Wire shapes sourced from ~/.grok/docs/user-guide/10-hooks.md and dcg's own HookProtocol::Grok doc comments. Native 'veil install --grok' remains a separate, optional ergonomics improvement -- Grok already reads ~/.claude/settings.json directly, so the existing install path is now sufficient for functional support.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text: Zac reports (2026-08-31): this is worse than a missing native install path -- Grok currently can't use filesystem tools at all when veil is installed. Not just 'no clean doctor output via the compatibility layer' as originally scoped; veil appears to be actively blocking/breaking Grok's filesystem tool calls, likely because Grok is routed through the Claude-Code-compatible hook path (~/.claude/settings.json PreToolUse) and veil's hook response/protocol isn't matching what Grok's compatibility layer expects, or Grok's tool-call shape doesn't map to what veil's hook logic checks. Needs investigation into what veil's hook returns when invoked from a Grok session (via the compat layer) vs a native Claude Code session -- suspect a hook decision/format mismatch causing veil to deny or the Grok layer to misinterpret the response, not just an ergonomics gap. Bumping priority given this is a functional break, not a nice-to-have.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE (confirmed from source, 2026-08-31):

src/types.rs L21-25: HookProtocol enum is exactly {ClaudeCode, GeminiCli, GitHubCopilot, Unknown} -- no Grok variant exists at all.

src/hook.rs parse_hook_input (L35-54): detects protocol by payload shape --
- is_claude_payload: hook_event_name=="PreToolUse" + tool_name + tool_input present
- is_gemini_payload: hook_event_name=="BeforeTool" (or explicit gemini marker) + snake_case tool_name/tool_input
- is_copilot_payload: toolName + toolArgs (camelCase) present
- none match -> Err("unsupported hook payload: could not detect Claude Code, Gemini CLI, or GitHub Copilot")

Even if a Grok payload happens to match the ClaudeCode shape (since dcg's docs say Grok is piped through the Claude-Code compatibility layer), normalize_tool_kind (L175-217) for HookProtocol::ClaudeCode only accepts tool_name in {"read","grep","bash"} case-insensitively -- any other tool name (Grok's own filesystem tool identifiers, whatever they are) falls through to Err("unsupported Claude Code tool `{name}` in hook payload").

Either way the failure surfaces the same: parse_hook_input returns Err -> lib.rs run_with_io propagates it as io::Error -> main.rs dispatch() Err arm prints `veil: {err}` to stderr and returns ExitCode::from(2) (src/main.rs L9-17). A PreToolUse hook that exits nonzero is treated as a DENY by the calling harness, not fail-open. So every single Grok filesystem tool call -- Read, Bash, Grep, whatever Grok calls them -- gets hard-blocked the moment veil's hook fires, because veil can never successfully classify the payload as one of its three known protocols/tool-name vocabularies. This is a categorical failure, not a soft ergonomics gap: "no native --grok install path" was the wrong frame for the original bead title.

Fix requires:
1. Determine what payload shape Grok's Claude-Code-compat layer actually emits on PreToolUse (event name, tool_name value(s), tool_input vs toolArgs casing) -- may need to capture one real payload from a Grok session.
2. Add a Grok arm to is_*_payload detection (or extend is_claude_payload's disambiguation if Grok truly reuses the exact Claude Code shape) and a corresponding branch in normalize_tool_kind mapping Grok's tool names to ToolKind::{Read,Grep,Bash}.
3. Add a HookProtocol::Grok variant (or confirm Grok payloads are byte-identical to Claude Code's and just need tool-name aliases added to the existing ClaudeCode arm).
4. Only after that does a native 'veil install --grok' writing ~/.grok/hooks/veil.json become meaningful -- right now even the compat-layer path is broken, so the native install path would just move where the same unsupported-payload failure occurs.

This confirms and sharpens the original bead: it's a missing protocol adapter, not missing install ergonomics.

title: Track B: sandbox architecture decision record (seatbelt + Landlock + broker)
description:
Parent: Veil v1 epic. Blocks all other Track B beads.

DECISION TO RECORD (in docs/plan.md, revise in place): 'veil sandbox -- <harness cmd>' launches the agent harness (claude, codex, gemini) as a child with protected paths unreadable at the OS level. macOS: sandbox-exec with a generated seatbelt profile (deny file-read* for protected globs; allow everything else by inheriting the default profile). Linux: Landlock ruleset via the landlock crate (LANDLOCK_ACCESS_FS_READ_FILE denied on protected dirs). Spine tools cannot run inside the sandbox (they must read the files), so 'veil exec <tool> <args>' talks over a unix socket to a broker daemon that veil sandbox started BEFORE entering the sandbox; the broker validates tool in [spine] authorized_tools, rejects shell strings, runs the tool with operator permissions, streams stdout/stderr back, and writes an audit entry. Hooks keep running inside the sandbox for UX and audit (enforcement:'sandbox').

RISKS TO RECORD: sandbox-exec is deprecated but functional on macOS 26; Endpoint Security needs entitlements (out of scope); seatbelt globs vs symlinks (resolve at profile build time and deny both); Landlock needs kernel >= 5.13 and ABI checks; broker socket must be 0600 and namespaced per session; the harness may spawn helper processes that inherit the sandbox (that is the point).

ALTERNATIVES REJECTED: FUSE overlay (too invasive), ptrace (slow, fragile), LD_PRELOAD (bypassable by static binaries).

OUTPUT: plan.md section + a sequence diagram; no code.

AMBITION ROUND ADDITIONS (2026-09-02): the ADR must also record the label model (public < derived < protected; agent clearance = derived; broker clearance = protected; outputs labelled by declared tool output class; copies take the join) and the per-adversary threat table (A0 accidental, A1 prompt-injected, A2 adversarial agent, A3 compromised host) from docs/plan.md, and state which track defeats which adversary. Every README claim must cite a row.

title: Document Veil boundary for path guard versus outbound content screening
description: Document the hard boundary between Veil's path guard and outbound content screening. Veil blocks sensitive raw reads and can help screen attachments or referenced files, but outbound body/disclosure policy belongs in the calling wrapper and later KOVREX integration. Make that split explicit so future contributors do not bend Veil into the wrong abstraction.

The resend/send boundary is described as a wrapper concern, not a generic Veil hook concern. 3. Attachment and file-reference checks are called out as legitimate Veil use cases. 4. Future KOVREX integration is framed as upstream/downstream of Veil, not inside Veil by default.
